rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for a sudden loss of composure or courage in a frightening situation.

example.english: The fire was so big that I was overcome with dismay and didn’t know what to do.
example.traditional: 見到火勢咁大，我即刻驚慌，唔知點算好。
example.jyutping: gin3 dou2 fo2 sai3 gam3 daai6 ngo5 zik1 hak1 ging1 fong1 m4 zi1 dim2 syun3 hou2

rows.note: Use 嚇親 as the all-purpose colloquial choice when dismay means causing fear or alarm.

example.english: The car nearly hit me just now, and that caused me dismay.
example.traditional: 頭先差啲畀架車撞到，真係嚇親我。
example.jyutping: tau4 sin1 caa1 di1 bei2 gaa3 ce1 zong6 dou3 zan1 hai6 haak3 can1 ngo5

rows.note: Use 打沉 when something demoralizes someone, leaving them sad, discouraged, or without energy.

example.english: Failing this exam was enough to dismay me.
example.traditional: 今次考試肥佬，真係打沉咗我。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 haau2 si3 fei4 lou2 zan1 hai6 daa2 cam4 zo2 ngo5

rows.traditional: 搞到 A 好唔開心
rows.jyutping: gaau2 dou3 A hou2 m4 hoi1 sam1
rows.note: Use this construction when the emphasis is on causing someone great emotional sadness or distress rather than fear.

example.english: You leaving without a word caused me great dismay.
example.traditional: 你唔聲唔聲咁走，搞到我好唔開心。
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 seng1 m4 seng1 gam3 zau2 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 hou2 m4 hoi1 sam1
